summary:
Public Law 118-181, the "Utah State Parks Adjustment Act" (H.R. 7332), enacted December 23, 2024, directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to convey specified federal land to the State of Utah for inclusion in three designated state parks. The Act operates through mandatory, no-consideration quitclaim conveyances subject to valid existing rights.

Section 2(a) requires the Secretary of the Interior, not later than 180 days after enactment, to convey all right, title, and interest of the United States in Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land identified for conveyance on the map titled "Antelope Island State Park Proposal: Utah State Park Additions" (dated February 28, 2023), for inclusion in Antelope Island State Park. The State bears all costs, including survey and administrative costs.

Section 2(b) imposes a parallel 180-day mandatory conveyance obligation on the Secretary of the Interior for BLM land identified on the map titled "Wasatch Mountain State Park Proposal Utah State Park Additions" (dated May 3, 2024), for inclusion in Wasatch Mountain State Park, with costs likewise borne by the State.

Section 2(c) requires the Secretary of Agriculture, within 180 days, to convey National Forest System land identified on the map titled "S. 2136—Utah State Parks Adjustment Act" (dated September 12, 2023), together with any improvements, for inclusion in Fremont Indian State Park. This conveyance carries several conditions: (1) the Secretary must reserve easements for all National Forest System roads and trails originating at, terminating at, or traversing the conveyed land (§2(c)(2)); (2) the Secretary shall convey only the specified water rights (Utah State Engineer database identifiers 63-44, 63-1607, and 63-2817) serving the Castle Rock Campground and Belknap Historic Guard Station interpretive site (§2(c)(3)); (3) the State shall pay reasonable costs of any survey the Secretary determines necessary to establish exact acreage and legal description (§2(c)(4)). Section 2(c)(5) grants the Secretary discretionary authority to enter into an agreement with the State on additional terms, including management of the Belknap site, road/trail use, continued permitted livestock grazing, Forest Service access to retained water rights, and other management-clarifying terms.

Section 2(d) authorizes either Secretary to make minor modifications to the applicable maps, including changes reflecting surveys.

Section 2(e) requires the State to use conveyed land for public purposes (parks, campgrounds, recreation, permitted livestock grazing) and establishes a reversionary interest: if a conveyed parcel ceases such use, it may, at the applicable Secretary's discretion, revert to the United States.

The Act contains no appropriations.
